issues.description: The script requests GM_xmlhttpRequest permission and @connect to cdn.jsdelivr.net, i.instagram.com, and raw.githubusercontent.com. However, all network requests are limited to Instagram's own API and trusted CDNs for resources and libraries. No evidence of user data or page content being sent to third-party servers.
issues.recommendation: Continue to monitor for any future changes that may introduce data exfiltration.

issues.description: The script requests a wide set of @grant permissions, including GM_openInTab, GM_notification, and GM_xmlhttpRequest, but not all are used in the visible code. This is a mild permission over-claim.
issues.recommendation: Restrict @grant to only those APIs actually used in the script.

issues.description: The script uses @require to load third-party libraries (mediabunny and jQuery) from official CDNs with SRI hashes, which mitigates supply chain risk.
issues.recommendation: Continue to pin versions and hashes for all external dependencies.

summary: The IG Helper script is generally safe. It does not exfiltrate user data, collect sensitive information, or execute remote code unsafely. All external resources are loaded from trusted CDNs with SRI hashes. There is mild permission over-claim, but no critical or high-severity risks detected.
